methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
DroneForge is a pre-seed stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector led by Chester Zelaya. The company has raised $2.5M to date. The comparable universe consists of five private companies operating in the same sector—Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air—though none provide direct valuation anchors at the pre-seed stage or adjacent funding rounds with sufficient data density for peer-median triangulation.

Given data limitations, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($2.5M) as a proxy for implied post-money value at pre-seed, a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding stage yields an implied valuation of $6.25M. This represents the median of the triangulated range.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5M to $7M, centered at $6M. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable transactions at identical or adjacent stages within the drones sector, which limits precision; the quality and specificity of the stage-progression multiplier itself; and execution risk inherent to early-stage asset development in a capital-intensive frontier technology sector. Additional comps or transaction data at seed and Series A stages would materially improve confidence in this range.
